6                 IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                    
7                     FOR THE DISTRICT OF ARIZONA                        

8                                                                        

9   BBK Tobacco & Foods LLP,           No. CV-19-05216-PHX-MTL           

10              Plaintiff,              ORDER                             

11   v.                                                                   

12   Central Coast Agriculture Incorporated, et                           
    al.,                                                                 
13                                                                        
               Defendants.                                               
14                                                                        
15        The Court has considered the briefing on Plaintiff BBK Tobacco & Foods LLP’s 
16   (“BBK”) Motion to Modify the Protective Order. (Doc. 566.)           
17        Years ago, at the beginning of this case, the Court entered a Protective Order to 
18   govern discovery shared between the parties. (Doc. 52.) Of concern to the parties and the 
19   Court alike was the overlapping nature of the parties’ businesses and the risk of disclosing 
20   proprietary financial information. See Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(c)(1)(G). The Protective Order 
21   thus contains a “Highly Confidential” attorneys’-eyes-only provision that excludes most 
22   party representatives from viewing documents of proprietary value.   
23        BBK now seeks to modify the Protective Order allowing its founder and owner 
24   Joshua Kesselman to view a chart of Defendant Central Coast Agriculture Incorporated’s 
25   (“CCA”)  revenues  over  several  years.  CCA  designated  this  material  as  Highly 
26   Confidential, and it is subject to the heightened protection of the Protective Order. BBK 
27   argues  that  the  proposed  modification  facilitates  Mr.  Kesselman  participating  in  the 
28   upcoming  mediation.  CCA  opposes  the  motion  because  divulging  this  proprietary 
 1 ||  information to Mr. Kesselman poses a  business risk since BBK may expand its operations 
2||    into the cannabis market, should cannabis become legal under federal law. CCA further 
  □□  argues that BBK’s general counsel may review Highly Confidential material, and he will 
4||    adequately advise his client at the mediation. 
5          “[D]istrict courts have inherent authority to grant a motion to modify a protective 
  ||  order where ‘good cause’ is shown. A party asserting good cause bears the burden to show 
  ||  that specific prejudice or harm will result if the motion is not granted.” CBS Interactive, 
  ||  Inc. v. Etilize, Inc., 257 F.R.D.  195, 201  (N.D. Cal. 2009) (citing Phillips ex rel. Ests. of 
9||    Byrd v. General Motors Corp., 307 F.3d 1206, 1213 (9th Cir. 2002)) (citation modified). 
10          The Court finds that BBK has not satisfied its burden. Of primary concern is the risk 
  ||  of competitive injury to CCA if the revenue numbers are misused by Mr. Kesselman, other 
      BBK personnel, or otherwise publicly disclosed. BBK’s argument that the information will 
13 |  be disclosed publicly at trial is of little concern for two reasons. First, the revenue numbers 
14]|    are relevant to an issue that will be tried to the Court, not a jury. Second, other provisions 
15 ||  in the Protective Order as well as the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure address the use of 
  ||  highly confidential information at trial and offer procedural protections, e.g., filing under 
  ||  seal. And, finally, BBK’s general counsel has access to these numbers and can advise Mr. 
18 ||  Kesselman adequately during the mediation. 
19          IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED that the Motion to Modify the Protective Order 
  ||  (Doc. 566) is DENIED. 
21          Dated this 5th day of August, 2025. 
22 
°°                                      Wichal  T.  Hburde 
24                                                 Michael T. Liburdi 
25                                             United  States District Judge
